standard_prerequisites.name: Points of a scheme over a field and of a fibre product: morphisms from the spectrum of a field to X correspond to pairs consisting of a point and an embedding of its residue field, and points of X times_S X correspond to quadruples with a prime ideal in the tensor product of the two residue fields
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited as a schemes chapter lemma at proof lines 1826, 1848, 1858 and 1872-1874
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the dictionary that converts the morphism-counting condition (1) and the diagonal condition (4) into the pointwise statements (2) and (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibre products and base change of the diagonal, and the definition of universally injective as base change being injective on points
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies sections of a base change with points of the fibre and turns injectivity of base changes into the diagonal being a section of an injective morphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: Purely inseparable field extensions in terms of uniqueness of embeddings into a common extension field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the field-theoretic step that two different embeddings produce two different morphisms from the spectrum of a field, and conversely.

core_obligations: Show (2) implies (1): a section of the base change over the spectrum of a field is the same as a point of the fibre with residue field equal to that field, so two morphisms over the same field give two such sections, which injectivity of the base change forces to coincide (proof lines 1812-1818).

Show (1) implies (2): given two points of a base change mapping to the same point of the base, choose a field containing both residue fields compatibly with the residue field of the base, obtain two morphisms from that field into X, use condition (1) to make them equal after composition to X, and conclude that the two points coincide (proof lines 1820-1836).

Show (1) and (2) imply (3): two distinct points over the same point of the base violate (2), and a non-purely-inseparable residue field extension produces a field over which the residue field has two embeddings, giving two distinct morphisms from that field and violating (1) (proof lines 1838-1851).

Show (3) implies (1): assuming f is radicial, a morphism from the spectrum of a field is a pair of a point and an embedding of its residue field, and radicality says exactly that the map forgetting the point is injective, which is condition (1) (proof lines 1853-1863).

Prove the equivalence with (4): a point of the fibre product is a quadruple including a prime ideal in the tensor product of the two residue fields; if f is universally injective then the diagonal, being a section of an injective morphism after base change to X, must be surjective, and conversely surjectivity of the diagonal forces the two points to be equal with a unique such prime ideal, hence purely inseparable residue field extensions, and base change of the surjective diagonal makes f universally injective (proof lines 1865-1884).
proof_roadmap: Identify condition (1) with injectivity of base changes to spectra of fields through the section/point dictionary, giving the equivalence of (1) and (2) (proof lines 1812-1836).

Connect both to radicality by the field-theoretic criterion for purely inseparable extensions (proof lines 1838-1863), and finally relate all three to surjectivity of the diagonal through the description of points of the fibre product and base change of the diagonal (proof lines 1865-1884).
difficulty_reason: The lemma assembles the four standard characterizations of a universally injective (equivalently radicial) morphism: injectivity of the induced maps on field-valued points, universal injectivity, radicality, and surjectivity of the diagonal (statement lines 1794-1810). The counted proof is a chain of four implications plus the diagonal equivalence, and it is not a citation: it uses the section/point dictionary for base changes to the spectrum of a field, the choice of a common field containing two residue fields to detect non-injectivity, the criterion for purely inseparable extensions by uniqueness of embeddings, and finally the description of points of the fibre product by quadruples involving a prime ideal in a tensor product of residue fields (proof lines 1812-1884). It is H2: the proof is long and has to keep four conditions in play, but every step is carried out in the counted span and the inputs are standard, so no independent research-level claim is made.
